result.title: Rank-1 Weight-Corrected Trainable Weight Averaging for Out-of-Distribution Detection
result.comment: Accepted to ACCV2026 Workshop on Subspaces in the Era of Foundation Models
result.summary: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection identifies inputs outside the training distribution. Rank-based analyses such as RankFeat and RankWeight suggest that OOD overconfidence is closely related to dominant low-rank components in feature and weight spaces. Since weight averaging operates directly in parameter space and improves model generalization, we consider it for OOD detection from a dominant-component perspective. Trainable Weight Averaging (TWA) assigns a single coefficient to each checkpoint, limiting independent control of dominant weight components. We extend TWA with leading rank-one weight components extracted by Singular Value Decomposition as correction directions, whose contributions are learned through the in-distribution classification objective. On ResNet50, our method improves over fine-tuning and standard TWA across the evaluated datasets with MSP and RankWeight, both with and without Outlier Exposure. Mahalanobis-based evaluation yields mixed results, indicating that the benefit depends on the OOD scoring protocol. Target-layer analyses with MSP and Energy favor correction near the classifier.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向 OOD 检测扩展可训练权重平均（TWA）：用 SVD 提取的前若干个 rank-1 权重分量作为修正方向，并以分布内分类目标学习各方向系数，在 ResNet50 上配合 MSP、RankWeight 打分优于微调与标准 TWA，Mahalanobis 评测结果不一致。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按方向学习系数」而非单一全局系数的做法，可能为 LVR 中按分量分配 latent 表示贡献与监督提供线索；但该工作作用于参数空间与 OOD 打分，与视觉推理状态无直接联系，需核查可迁移性。
